canonical_statement: Acute treatment included aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation, dopamine, teicoplamin as printed in the first treatment paragraph, and clindamycin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The treatment included aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation, administration of dopamine, and antimicrobial agent therapy with teicoplamin and clindamycin.

canonical_statement: The outcome was reported as favorable; a diffuse macular rash appeared on day 2, acute renal failure and other laboratory abnormalities resolved, and extensive peeling of both hands developed by day 5.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The treatment outcome was favorable. On the second day, a diffuse cutaneous macular rash appeared. The acute renal failure and the biological abnormalities resolved. On the fifth day, the patient was transferred back to the hospital where she had undergone surgery; extensive peeling then developed on both of the patient’s hands.

The authors state that the patient met toxic shock syndrome criteria and that the diagnosis of staphylococcal TSS was confirmed by bacteriologic results.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our patient met the criteria of TSS: she had fever, rash, desquamation, hypotension, vomiting, diarrhea, myalgias, elevated creatine kinase, acute renal failure, and thrombocytopenia. The diagnosis of staphylococcal TSS was confirmed by bacteriologic results.

canonical_statement: The authors claim that this was the first European case of TSS due to TSST-1-producing MRSA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: this case is the first of TSS due to TSST-1–producing MRSA in Europe.

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that the possibility of MRSA must be considered when initiating antimicrobial agents to treat toxic shock syndrome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The possibility of MRSA must be considered when initiating antimicrobial agents to treat TSS.
